APIM APIOps
inside the workshop

The complete configuration and request flow, with native commands, ownership boundaries and tested outcomes.

01

Architecture

The customer runs the native apiops CLI locally. Git records the configuration; APIM serves the API traffic; API Center stores the catalog. This guide explains the deployed workshop pattern, not a production landing zone.

The public repository supplies files and offline checks. Each participant chooses a tenant, subscription and dedicated resource group. No hosted deployment connects this repository to the author's Azure environment.

02

Components and rationale

ComponentRole in this workshopReason for the choice
Customer workstationNode.js, native APIOps CLI, Azure CLI, Git, curl and jq.Participants see each command and its result directly.
Microsoft Entra IDCustomer identity for Azure access.The customer signs in with az login and selects their subscription.
Resource groupGroups the workshop's Azure resources.A dedicated group makes resource review and eventual cleanup easier.
APIM ConsumptionOne gateway containing dev and QA API namespaces.A small sandbox for configuration and policy exercises. Consumption usage can incur charges.
API Center FreeCatalog metadata, versions, definitions and specifications.Exercises catalog backup and replay separately from gateway configuration.
httpbin.orgExternal echo endpoint used with synthetic requests.Demonstrates backend routing without deploying an application server.
GitHub repositoryDistributes artifacts, labs and presentation; checks content.Customers can clone it without access to the author's subscription.

Dev and QA share gateway capacity and the same service boundary. Prefixes prevent naming collisions; they do not create production isolation. No VNet, private endpoint, application database or observability service is provisioned by this workshop.

03

Native command lifecycle

  1. Authenticate and provision: copy .env.example, set customer values, run az login and select the subscription. Azure CLI creates or selects the resources.
  2. Prepare configuration: use the supplied apim-artifacts/ files, or extract a selected baseline. JSON stores information, XML stores policies, and OpenAPI describes operations.
  3. Preview and deploy: review apiops publish --dry-run, then publish with the dev or QA override file. A plan does not validate live backend behavior.
  4. Change and roll back: commit the release named-value change and publish that commit. Revert it in Git, then publish the revert commit. --commit-id compares a commit with its parent; it is not a general missed-deployment detector.
  5. Verify: use curl and jq to inspect status, echo and response headers. The release lab polls for gateway propagation before asserting the result.

An override-only commit produced zero incremental PUTs in the test. Lab 04 uses a full publish to apply that configuration change.

04

Request path and configuration

Request or artifactActual behavior
/{dev|qa}/orders/statusThe operation policy returns synthetic JSON and HTTP 200 directly. It sets X-Demo-Environment and X-Demo-Release on this response.
/{dev|qa}/orders/echoThe operation rewrites the path to /get. The configured backend is https://httpbin.org. The outbound policy fragment adds environment and release headers.
Environment overridesThe dev and QA files set name and path prefixes. QA overrides the release to v2 while the canonical artifact starts at v1.
Supporting resourcesProducts, tags, named values, backend references and policy fragments are configuration objects published with the API.
API Center filesThe default catalog workspace contains the Orders API, version v1 and its OpenAPI definition. The CLI publishes and extracts these independently of APIM.

Utilities and measured coverage

LabsCapabilityObserved result
02–04Publish, overrides, incremental changes, rollbackHTTP 200; dev v1 → v2 → v1, QA v2; one PUT for the release change.
05Extraction, filters, dependency expansion11 resources with dependencies versus 7 without; wildcard/exclusion and filtered publish passed.
06Secret redaction and rejectionA synthetic secret extracted as *** REDACTED ***; unresolved publish returned exit 2.
06Deletion and local cleanupOne disposable NamedValue DELETE in a pinned commit; stale extracted file removed. Full unmatched deletion was not applied to the fixture directory.
07API Center backup and replaySame-instance replay passed, including metadata-only variants with --no-specifications.
08Pipeline scaffoldingGitHub Actions and Azure DevOps files generated locally. Conflict exit 1 and --force verified; no hosted deployment.
09–10CLI diagnostics and runtime assertionsHelp, JSON output, debug logs, exit codes and endpoint checks passed.

Evidence: 18 literal customer command blocks passed on 25 October 2026 with @azure-tools/apiops-cli@1.0.5. The resources already existed for this validation; fresh creation and whole-group cleanup were not repeated. Interactive Copilot, Key Vault, other APIM tiers and all resource combinations are outside the measured coverage.

06

Identity and trust boundaries

BoundaryWorkshop behaviorCustomer responsibility
Workstation → Azure managementAPIOps uses DefaultAzureCredential. The labs use the Azure CLI session.Verify the selected tenant/subscription and effective identity. Other configured credential sources can take precedence.
Azure resource authorizationCommands operate on the resource names supplied by the customer.Obtain permissions for provisioning and managing APIM/API Center from your administrator.
Git → local configuration.env and .work/ are ignored by Git.Keep credentials and raw diagnostic logs out of public commits. Review extracted artifacts for sensitive content.
Client → APIM → external backendThe synthetic sample has no subscription-key authentication and uses a public echo service.Send synthetic data only and decide appropriate API authentication before adapting the sample.
Generated pipeline → AzureThe workshop generates local examples only.Choose and configure a separate identity and approval model if enabling deployment automation later.
07

Customer decisions and workshop sequence

Before Lab 00: choose your tenant, subscription, allowed region, unique resource names and spending limit. West Europe is an editable example, not a residency decision for your organization.

Labs 00–02: install, sign in, provision or select a sandbox, then publish dev and QA. Labs 03–06: exercise change control and safeguards. Labs 07–10: inspect the catalog, generated automation and measured results. Lab 11: review and remove your dedicated resource group when finished.

1 Who owns the sandbox?

Confirm the subscription owner, permitted resource types, provisioning permissions and cost limits.

2 What changes before production?

Decide environment isolation, API authentication, approved backends, secret storage, private connectivity and operational monitoring against your requirements.

3 Will you enable automation?

If yes, choose a customer-owned repository, deployment identity, resource scope and approval process. Nothing in this workshop connects that path automatically.
